record.context_brief: Direct three-α decay of the Hoyle state
record.original_question: Can a direct three-α decay branch of the carbon-12 Hoyle state be experimentally observed, despite current searches only limiting the branch relative to the 8Be + α two-body decay channel to about 10^-4 without success, and can such an observation give a clearer signal of the Hoyle state's internal α structure?

evidence.quote: For the moment the branching ratio with the two body decay, 8Be + α, is down to 10 −4 with still no success.
However, this does not mean that the experimental e ﬀort should be stopped! It would, indeed, be very nice if a dire ct three α decay could be found.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Hoyle state is the second 0⁺ excited state of the ¹²C nucleus, located near the 3α breakup threshold and known to decay predominantly through the sequential channel ¹²C* → ⁸Be(g.s.) + α → 3α. A direct three-body breakup channel ¹²C* → 3α (in which the three α particles are emitted simultaneously, not via an intermediate ⁸Be ground state) is also kinematically allowed and is regarded as a sensitive probe of an underlying α-cluster (in particular, dilute α-condensate-like) structure of the Hoyle state.

Let Γ_{3α,direct} denote the partial width for the direct three-α decay of the Hoyle state and let Γ denote its total width (equivalently, let Γ_{8Be+α} be the partial width of the sequential channel). Define the direct branching ratio
    B_direct = Γ_{3α,direct} / Γ   (or, equivalently, Γ_{3α,direct} / Γ_{8Be+α} to leading order).

Existing experimental searches have, at the time of formulation, established only upper bounds B_direct ≲ 10⁻⁴ relative to the sequential ⁸Be + α channel, with no positive observation.

Problem. Determine whether a nonzero direct three-α decay branch of the Hoyle state can be experimentally observed (i.e., whether B_direct > 0 can be established at a statistically significant level), and assess whether such an observation, together with the kinematical correlations of the three outgoing α particles, provides a quantitative discriminator of the internal α-cluster structure of the Hoyle state.
artifact.category_tag: Nuclear cluster physics / Hoyle state decay
artifact.status_search_result: No positive observation of a direct 3α decay of the Hoyle state has been reported. Subsequent experiments have only tightened the upper bound: Phys. Rev. C 101, 021302 (2020) reports Γ_{3α}/Γ < 5.7 × 10⁻⁶, and a 2018 analysis improved the limit to < 0.026% (95% C.L.). Thus the question of whether a direct 3α branch exists, and what it would reveal about the Hoyle state's α-cluster structure, remains experimentally open.

status_evidence.title: A stringent upper limit on the direct 3α decay of the Hoyle State in ¹²C
status_evidence.snippet: Upper limit Γ_{3α}/Γ < 5.7 × 10⁻⁶ on direct 3α decay branching of the Hoyle state.
status_evidence.claim: Searches continue to provide only upper limits, with no positive detection of a direct 3α branch.

status_evidence.title: Stringent upper limit on the direct decay of the Hoyle state in ¹²C
status_evidence.snippet: Published 2020 result tightening the upper bound on the direct 3α decay branching ratio.
status_evidence.claim: State-of-the-art bound is far below 10⁻⁴ but the direct branch has not been observed.

status_evidence.title: An improved upper limit on the direct 3α decay of the Hoyle state
status_evidence.snippet: Improved limit < 0.026% (95% C.L.), a factor of 5 better than previous limit.
status_evidence.claim: Continued experimental effort has only improved upper limits without observing the direct decay.
